subject: computer-science
title: Computer Systems: Inside the CPU
welcome_lead: Open the case and trace data through the CPU's components.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on CPU components, buses and memory hierarchy.
final_note: You now understand how the CPU works with memory to run programs.

concepts.def: Central processing unit — runs program instructions.
Arithmetic logic unit — does maths and logic.
Control unit — directs operations inside the CPU.
Tiny, very fast store inside the CPU.
Small, fast memory near the CPU for hot data.
Set of wires that carry data between parts.

walkthroughs.body_html: The CU fetches an instruction from memory and decodes it. If it's a maths op, the ALU does the calculation. Results go into a register.

• Address bus: which memory location?
  • Data bus: the actual data
  • Control bus: signals like read/write
From fastest+smallest to slowest+largest: Registers → Cache (L1, L2, L3) → RAM → Storage (SSD/HDD). Closer to the CPU = faster but more expensive.

mcqs.q: Which CPU component performs maths and logic?
Which bus tells memory whether to read or write?
